# Daniel Mejía R.

> Physicist and full-stack software engineer. Builds AI-enabled services, from machine learning pipelines to LLM-enabled AI systems.

## Pages
- [About Me](https://daniel-m.github.io/about/)
- [Blog](https://daniel-m.github.io/posts/)
- [Now](https://daniel-m.github.io/now/)

## Posts
- [A second look to Multer DOS](https://daniel-m.github.io/2026/11/a-second-look-to-multer-dos/): Revisiting multer-dos, a Multer storage engine for DigitalOcean Spaces, with added TypeScript support and dependency updates after noticing about 10 weekly npm downloads.
- [Some fun computing the short distance between two curves](https://daniel-m.github.io/2026/11/some-fun-computing-the-short-distance-between-two-curves/): Derives the shortest straight-line distance between two curves, showing it is perpendicular to both at its endpoints, with worked examples for a parabola and line and for eˣ and ln x.
- [Project Euler - Problem 2 - Even Fibonacci Numbers](https://daniel-m.github.io/2026/08/project-euler-problem-2-even-fibonacci-numbers/): Solves Project Euler problem 2 by deriving a recurrence and a generating function for the even Fibonacci numbers, then timing both approaches.
- [Project Euler - Problem 1 - Multiples of 3 and 5](https://daniel-m.github.io/2026/08/project-euler-problem-1-multiples-of-3-and-5/): Project Euler problem 1 is solved by brute force and by Gauss sums, and an AI-generated solution passed its unit tests while still giving a wrong answer.
- [Reflections on blogging in AI era - 2026](https://daniel-m.github.io/2026/08/reflections-on-blogging-in-ai-era-2026/): After a career break, the author rethinks why they code and blog, vowing to keep coding without AI and to write human critiques of AI-generated content.
- [Python Generators Iterator](https://daniel-m.github.io/2023/11/python-generators-iterator/): Notes on Python generator iterators: how yield suspends and resumes functions, how classes implementing __iter__ and __next__ act as iterators, and why this streams data within limited memory.
- [Jupyter Kernels with Pyenv](https://daniel-m.github.io/2023/08/jupyter-kernels-with-pyenv/): Shows how to register a pyenv virtualenv as a Jupyter kernel by installing jupyterlab and ipykernel in it and running ipykernel install --user.
- [ExpressJS uploads to Digital Ocean Spaces through S3 AWS-S3](https://daniel-m.github.io/2022/06/expressjs-uploads-to-digital-ocean-spaces-through-s3-aws-s3/): A short account of building multer-dos, a custom multer storage engine that uploads files to DigitalOcean Spaces via the S3 API after multer-s3 failed, and has run in production for a year.
- [Dealing with scammers using Selenium and Python](https://daniel-m.github.io/2022/05/dealing-with-scammers-using-selenium-and-python/): A proof-of-concept Selenium bot fills a phishing site's credit card form with random data to flood the scammers' database with junk.
- [Managing python versions and virtual environments with pyenv](https://daniel-m.github.io/2021/11/managing-python-versions-and-virtual-environments-with-pyenv/): A practical guide to installing pyenv on Debian, configuring the shell, and using pyenv-virtualenv to manage Python versions and isolated environments.
- [Installing InfluxDB with High Availability](https://daniel-m.github.io/2020/10/installing-influxdb-with-high-availability/): Guide to running high-availability InfluxDB 1.8 on three Debian nodes, using influxdb-relay for replicated writes and nginx for load balancing.
- [Configuring a minimal MongoDB Replica Set with authentication](https://daniel-m.github.io/2020/10/configuring-a-minimal-mongodb-replica-set-with-authentication/): Step-by-step guide to configuring a three-node MongoDB 4.4 replica set on Debian with a shared keyfile, authentication, and admin users.
- [Character encodings and a bit of Python](https://daniel-m.github.io/2020/02/character-encodings-and-a-bit-of-python/): Notes on character encodings explaining how Unicode code points map to UTF-8, UTF-16, and UTF-32 bytes, with Python examples and base64 for binary data.
- [A mystery using Python hashlib to calculate checksums](https://daniel-m.github.io/2020/02/a-mystery-using-python-hashlib-to-calculate-checksums/): Explains computing file checksums with Python hashlib in chunks, and why reusing one hasher object across requests produced wrong digests.
- [NVIDIA Optimus: A tale of two graphic cards](https://daniel-m.github.io/2019/11/nvidia-optimus-a-tale-of-two-graphic-cards/): A practical guide to making NVIDIA Optimus laptops work on Debian Testing using Bumblebee, module blacklists, and scripts to switch the NVIDIA GPU on and off.
- [Google's BigQuery and Go](https://daniel-m.github.io/2019/02/googles-bigquery-and-go/): Notes on Google BigQuery covering its serverless architecture, projects, datasets, tables, views, partitions, jobs, and schemas, plus why nested columns often beat lookup tables.
- [Notes on Go concurrency](https://daniel-m.github.io/2019/01/notes-on-go-concurrency/): Notes on concurrency models and OS primitives, then Go goroutines, with sync.WaitGroup examples for waiting until they finish.
- [ESP32: Blinking a LED](https://daniel-m.github.io/2018/12/esp32-blinking-a-led/): Shows how to blink an LED on the ESP32 using esp-idf GPIO calls, then moves the loop into a FreeRTOS task created with xTaskCreate.
- [ESP32: esp-idf Development Framework and the FreeRTOS kernel](https://daniel-m.github.io/2018/11/esp32-esp-idf-development-framework-and-the-freertos-kernel/): Overview of the esp-idf configure-build-flash-monitor workflow and FreeRTOS basics on ESP32: memory, tasks, and why app_main() is the entry point.
- [ESP32: Setting up a development environment](https://daniel-m.github.io/2018/10/esp32-setting-up-a-development-environment/): Guide to installing the Espressif esp-idf toolchain and serial tools, then building, flashing, and monitoring hello-world on an ESP32.
- [Getting started with the ESP32](https://daniel-m.github.io/2018/10/getting-started-with-the-esp32/): First post in an ESP32 series explaining why this low-cost Wi-Fi and Bluetooth chip suits IoT projects, with a series table of contents.
- [Alternative blog at http://blog.parallelo.ai](https://daniel-m.github.io/2018/10/alternative-blog-at-http--blog.parallelo.ai/): Short pointer post directing readers to the author's work-related blog at blog.parallelo.ai, since this site is no longer actively updated.
- [Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery Systems On The Cloud](https://daniel-m.github.io/2018/08/continuous-integration-and-continuous-delivery-systems-on-the-cloud/): Compares Jenkins, GoCD, CircleCI, Travis-CI and AWS CodePipeline for continuous integration and delivery, covering how each one runs and integrates with source control.
- [An Overview of Go Web Frameworks](https://daniel-m.github.io/2018/06/an-overview-of-go-web-frameworks/): Compares Go web routers and frameworks like chi, echo, httprouter, and gorilla/mux by GitHub stats and fit for REST APIs, favoring chi and echo.
- [ImageNet: VGGNet, ResNet, Inception, and Xception with Keras](https://daniel-m.github.io/2018/06/imagenet-vggnet-resnet-inception-and-xception-with-keras/): Notes on ImageNet CNN architectures (VGG16/19, ResNet50, Inception V3, Xception) covering their key ideas, Keras input sizes, and weight serialization.
- [Notes on Python multiprocessing](https://daniel-m.github.io/2018/03/notes-on-python-multiprocessing/): Notes on Python's multiprocessing package, covering `Pool.map` for parallel execution, the `__main__` guard, and functor wrappers for multi-argument functions.
- [The GeoJSON Format](https://daniel-m.github.io/2018/02/the-geojson-format/): Notes on the GeoJSON format (RFC 7946) covering geometry and feature types, WGS 84 [longitude, latitude] coordinates, and splitting shapes at the antimeridian.
- [Python Web Frameworks: An Overview of Django vs Flask vs Tornado vs Pyramid](https://daniel-m.github.io/2018/01/python-web-frameworks-an-overview-of-django-vs-flask-vs-tornado-vs-pyramid/): Compares Python web frameworks Flask, Django, Tornado, and Pyramid, covering their design philosophies, community size, and best-fit project types.
- [Old Blog](https://daniel-m.github.io/2018/01/old-blog/): Pointer to the author's dormant Blogspot blog, Daniel's log book, which holds many unpublished drafts the author plans to publish.
